constructionSteps.title: Four coplanar floor rails, retained supports, connected base and mounted SPIKE hub
Six-socket motor cradle and four retained support posts
Two separated passive bearings and their connected support cage
Blue driven rocker, orange passive rotor, retained shafts and grooved band anchors
Balanced wheel masses, two matched 33 mm bands, cable and saved-pose alignment

notes: The output is a genuinely passive balanced rotor on two retained round-bore bearings.
The two matched bands act on opposite 8 mm lever arms, so their pretension is balanced at reset.
3713 bushes provide real 7 LDU waists and two 9 LDU flanges. They are keyed to the rockers, not independent pulleys.
Paired retained parallel shafts physically lock each thin anchor bridge to its two rocker layers; native locked-hinges diagnostics are expected and preserved if emitted.
Band stiffness and damping are the unchanged native approximation, not measured properties of a physical rubber band.
The prototype includes the actual mounted SPIKE hub and explicit motor A, so VM/controller timing matches the final machine.

bandRetention.note: Bands sit in the waist between the actual 3713 flanges. Both central shaft tips stop at Y=-50, 8 LDU below the complete band tube envelope.

frameInterfaces.supportPurpose: Four coplanar floor rails support the complete connected frame, including the hub, without fixing any body in the final simulation.
frameInterfaces.cable: The fixed motor cable is integral to the motor. Connect port A on the fixed hub; route it along the frame below both rocker layers and away from the band and wheel sweep. The cable is not a separately simulated rigid part.
